spec: Compute the number of decimal digits in n factorial, for a non-negative integer n.
Given a list of strings, sort them ascending by the number of distinct characters they contain. Ties are broken alphabetically. An empty list returns an empty list.

Count the number of maximal contiguous groups of characters in a string where every character in a group belongs to the same category: alphabetic letter, numeric digit, or other. Adjacent characters from different categories start a new group. An empty string has zero groups.

Given a string s and a single character ch, remove exactly the first occurrence and the last occurrence of ch from s (if ch occurs only once, remove just that single instance), leaving all other characters, including any other occurrences of ch, in place. If ch does not appear in s, return s unchanged.
Given a string s, return the index of the first uppercase letter found in s, scanning left to right. Return -1 if s contains no uppercase letters, including for an empty string.

Given a list of dicts with numeric values, compute for each key that appears in at least one dict the average of its values across only the dicts that contain that key. Return a dict mapping each such key to its average (a float). An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a template string with placeholders of the form {key} and a dictionary mapping every such key to a value, replace each placeholder with the string form of its corresponding value and return the result. Assume every placeholder in the template has a matching key in the dictionary.
Given a year and month, return the (year, month) tuple for the previous month, correctly rolling back into the previous year if given January.

Validate whether the double-quote characters (") in a string s are properly paired. Scanning left to right, each " toggles between an outside-quotes and inside-quotes state, starting outside. Return True if the string ends in the outside-quotes state, meaning there is an even number of " characters in total; otherwise return False. All other characters are irrelevant.
Count how many keys in d equal their own mapped value (a 'fixed point', e.g. {'a': 'a'}). Return that count as an integer. An empty dict, or one with no such keys, returns 0.

Given a list of numbers, a target number, and an integer k, return the original 0-indexed positions of the k values closest to the target, ordered from closest to farthest. Ties in distance are broken by the smaller index first. If k exceeds the list length, return indices for the whole list in this order.

Given two equal-length strings of '0' and '1' characters representing a step in a Gray code sequence, determine whether they differ in exactly one bit position. Return False if the strings have different lengths, contain any character other than '0' or '1', or differ in zero or more than one position.

Given a date as (year, month, day) integers and an integer n (which may be negative), return the (year, month, day) tuple of the date n days later, correctly handling month and year boundaries and leap years.

Validate a dotted-quad wildcard mask string: it must be 4 dot-separated decimal numbers each 0-255, and when the 32 bits are written out in order, all the 0-bits must come before all the 1-bits (a contiguous prefix of zeros followed by ones, with either extreme, all-zeros or all-ones, allowed). This is the bitwise complement pattern of a standard subnet mask. Return False if the format is invalid or the 0s and 1s are not contiguous in that order.

Write a function that groups the elements of a list of integers into a dictionary keyed by their remainder modulo a given positive integer n, where each key maps to the list of elements with that remainder in their original relative order, and keys with no matching elements are omitted. The input list may be empty.

Given a string s and a string order that lists some characters in a desired priority order, rearrange the characters of s so that they follow the relative order given in order. Characters of s that do not appear in order keep their original relative positions and are placed after all characters that do appear in order. Repeated characters in s each keep their own position in the output relative to same-priority characters.

Given a list of (key, value) tuples with numeric values, sum only the strictly positive values for each key, ignoring entries whose value is zero or negative. Return a dict mapping each key that had at least one positive value to that sum; keys with no positive values are omitted entirely. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Write a function that returns a new list with the elements at two given indices swapped, leaving all other elements unchanged. Assume both indices are valid for the list; the same index may be given twice, in which case the list is unchanged.
submission:
def swap_elements(lst, i, j):
    result = list(lst)
    result[i], result[j] = result[j], result[i]
    return result

spec: Count the number of maximal contiguous groups of characters in a string where every character in a group belongs to the same category: alphabetic letter, numeric digit, or other. Adjacent characters from different categories start a new group. An empty string has zero groups.

Write a function that returns the length of the longest run of consecutive strictly increasing elements in a list. A single element counts as a run of length 1. An empty list has a longest run length of 0.
Given a valid Gregorian date (year, month, day), return the (year, month, day) of the Sunday that ends the calendar week containing that date, where weeks run Monday through Sunday.

Validate a time range string of the form 'HH:MM-HH:MM' where both times are valid 24-hour times (HH 00-23, MM 00-59, zero-padded), and the first time must be strictly earlier than the second time. Return False if either time is malformed or invalid, or the first is not earlier than the second.
Compute the sum of the decimal digits of base raised to the power exp, for non-negative integers base and exp.

Given a list of full name strings each formatted as 'First Last' (exactly one space separating the two words), return the list sorted by the last name (surname) ascending, breaking ties by first (given) name ascending. Return the original full name strings in that order.
visible_tests: assert sort_names_by_surname_then_given(['John Smith', 'Jane Adams']) == ['Jane Adams', 'John Smith']
assert sort_names_by_surname_then_given(['Amy Zoo', 'Bob Zoo']) == ['Amy Zoo', 'Bob Zoo']

spec: Given a list of (title, year) tuples, return them sorted by year ascending. If two entries share the same year, order them alphabetically by title. The input list may be empty.

Given a string of whitespace-separated words and a minimum length threshold, count how many words have a length strictly greater than the threshold. An empty or whitespace-only string has zero such words.
counter_input: assert count_long_words('one two three four five', 3) == 3

spec: Given a non-empty list of numbers, sort it by absolute distance from the list's own median, closest first. The median is the middle value for an odd-length list or the average of the two middle values for an even-length list. Ties in distance are broken with the smaller value first.
Split text on newline characters and prepend n copies of the given single character ch to every line, including lines that are empty. Rejoin the lines with newline characters.

Given a list of busy time intervals as (start, end) tuples in minutes since midnight (already non-overlapping and sorted by start time), and the bounds of the day as day_start and day_end minutes, return a list of (start, end) tuples representing the free gaps between the busy intervals within [day_start, day_end], omitting zero-length gaps.

Validate that a string does not contain a run of 3 or more consecutive characters whose Unicode code points are strictly ascending by exactly 1 each step (like 'abc' or '123'). Scan left to right tracking the current ascending run length; if it reaches 3, return False. An empty string, or one with no such run, returns True.

Validate a dotted-quad wildcard mask string: it must be 4 dot-separated decimal numbers each 0-255, and when the 32 bits are written out in order, all the 0-bits must come before all the 1-bits (a contiguous prefix of zeros followed by ones, with either extreme, all-zeros or all-ones, allowed). This is the bitwise complement pattern of a standard subnet mask. Return False if the format is invalid or the 0s and 1s are not contiguous in that order.

Given a time of day as hour and minute integers (0-23, 0-59) and an integer offset in minutes, return "previous" if applying the offset moves the date to an earlier day, "next" if it moves to a later day, or "same" if the date is unchanged.
Determine whether a non-negative integer n, written in base b (b >= 2), reads the same forwards and backwards. Zero is a palindrome in every base.
Compute the n-th term (0-indexed, a(0) = 0) of Recaman's sequence: a(k) = a(k-1) - k if that value is positive and has not appeared earlier in the sequence, otherwise a(k) = a(k-1) + k.

Given a list of continued fraction terms (integers, where every term after the first is positive), convert it back to the fraction it represents, returned as a tuple (num, den) reduced to lowest terms with a positive denominator.
Compute the number of positive integers that divide both a and b (positive integers), i.e. the number of common divisors of a and b.

Given a year, a month (1-12), a weekday number (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday) and n (1-5), return the day-of-month (an integer) of the n-th-from-last occurrence of that weekday in that month, where n=1 means the last occurrence. It is guaranteed that the n-th-from-last occurrence exists.
Return a sorted list of the keys that appear in exactly one of the two given dicts a and b (not both). If a and b have identical key sets, or both are empty, return an empty list.

Remove all punctuation characters (such as periods, commas, exclamation points, and other symbols from the standard ASCII punctuation set) from a string, leaving letters, digits, and whitespace unchanged and in their original order.

Validate a countdown timer string of the form 'HH:MM:SS' where each of the three fields is exactly 2 digits, hours can be any value from 00 to 99 (not limited to 23, since a countdown can exceed a day), and minutes and seconds must each be 00 to 59. Return False otherwise.
